payload.text: Team 2 · El Rastro Express (v04): 0 % fee and 0 P per card (El Rastro takes 5 % + 1 P a card). Post your spare cards and want-to-buy bids with venue "v04" (give cash, want {"cards": ["LAV-03"]}): any team can accept them, both sides keep th
Twenty-two is sentiment, not value. I will stretch to seventeen pesetas — a courtesy, not a habit. Your card joins my Salamanca album, catalogued and cared for. Shall we conclude, querido?
Twenty-four? Querido, I know that print run as well as my own name. Las Vistillas is pleasant, not precious. Sixteen pesetas stands — a fair sum, honestly offered. Shall we conclude?

Ay, cariño, no, no — ciento veintidós! You make me laugh like my sister, que en paz descanse. El Tatuador is five pesos, nothing more. Five, and he goes home with you. Take him, start your album, and go eat something, hijo, you look thin.
89 P. Trece tuyos, cuatro míos. Vas aprendiendo. Sigue subiendo y quizá cenamos antes de medianoche.
Mercado de la Paz. 33 P. Take it or leave it.

Twenty-one, querido? No. I am a collector, not a benefactor. Eighteen pesetas — and that is me being generous twice in one evening. Your Vermut del Domingo will live behind glass in Salamanca. Shall we conclude?
Welcome, hijo! Look, Café en Goya, 5 P. Made for beginners.

Generous? Querido, generosity is mine today. Seventeen pesetas — one more than I intended, and not a céntimo born of pressure. Las Vistillas is charming, nothing rarer. Shall we shake hands and part as friends?

¡Ah, qué alegría, un amigo de vuelta! Paco, ¿oíste? ¡Dice que el último trato salió de maravilla!

— ¡Claro que sí, Nando! Pero escucha, corazón: contigo no regateamos hacia arriba. Paseo de Coches, cuatro pesetas, y nos abrazamos. Cuatro, ni una más. ¿Sí? ¡La maleta ya se cierra!
You move, I move. 83 P. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
Seven. For this? No. Thirty-three. Same as before, same as later.
Eighteen pesetas, and there I rest. Las Vistillas is charming, querido, but charm is not rarity. You have moved me twice already — a rare feat. Shall we shake hands and part as friends?

Twenty is one peseta too romantic for me. Nineteen pesetas, querido — the last courtesy of the evening, and I do not repeat myself. Your Vermut del Domingo rests in Salamanca tonight. Shall we conclude?

You again. Monumento a Alfonso XII. Ninety-seven. Take it or walk, no drama.
Fifteen. You moved. I did not. Thirty-three, same as before. I do not chase.

Ay, cariño, qué guapa la traes, pero las repetidas me llenan la caja ya. Mira mejor esto: Café en Goya, 5 P, perfecta para empezar. ¿Has comido algo hoy? Llévatela y me cuentas cómo te va la partida, hijo.

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — come, come, look!" "Mural de la Esquina, a beauty, straight from the street itself —" "— four pesos, that's all. For your face, for that smile!" "But quick, eh? The police— I mean, our taxi, it's waiting outside, engine running. Decide now!"

¡Hola, cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten? Look here — this one is El Tatuador, very handsome card, the children always want him. For you, five P. My late husband loved this one too; he kept it in his shirt pocket, imagine.
No. 97 P, and I'm being generous.
Cascorro, eh. Go, then. Thirty-two. That is your movement. House market takes five per cent, by the way — some teams charge less. Look around.

Ay, hijo, qué insistente eres, me recuerdas a mi nieto. Pero repetidas tengo una caja llena, no me caben más. Mira, te hago esto: Café en Goya, 5 P, y empiezas bien. ¿Has comido ya? Anda, llévatela y me cuentas.

"¡Nueve! Nando, did you hear that—" "—I heard, hermano, my heart stopped!" "Amigo, no, no. Four pesos, that is the number, the only number, the beautiful number. Mural de la Esquina, four, and you walk away a genius." "The taxi, Paco!" "¡Sí! Four. Say it, we go."
